evidence: src/application/order-service.ts: export function assertCombineItemsRule throws DomainError("An order requires at least one item"), and the flag shows the same literal at src/domain/order.ts:27

src/application/order-service.ts: private combineItems checks `!item.productId || !Number.isInteger(item.quantity) || item.quantity <= 0` and throws "Each order item needs a product id and positive integer quantity", and the flag shows the same literal at src/domain/order.ts:30
src/application/order-service.ts placeOrder: `new Order(`order-${this.nextId++}`, items)` passes the items to the domain constructor, which presumably runs the same checks again
src/application/catalogue-service.ts: validateCombineItems(items: PlaceOrderDto["items"]) calls assertCombineItemsRule from order-service, putting an order rule in the catalogue service
Both services use only the injected ProductRepository/OrderRepository for persistence, so there is no repository bypass
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Persistence goes only through the injected repository ports (ProductRepository, OrderRepository), and dtos.ts is consistent. Order-service.ts fails the duplication criterion. It writes out the Order invariants as its own code instead of leaving them to the domain Order: the non-empty items check in assertCombineItemsRule and the per-item productId/positive-integer quantity check in combineItems. The candidate flags show the same error messages in src/domain/order.ts at lines 27 and 30. That points to the same guards existing in the Order constructor, so each invariant lives in two places. OrderService then passes the combined items to `new Order(...)`, which validates them again. I could not see the domain source, so this conclusion depends on those flagged lines being validation code, which the identical error texts strongly suggest. There is also a smaller cohesion problem: CatalogueService exposes validateCombineItems, an order rule taken from order-service.ts. Because it calls the shared function, it is not a copy, but it puts order validation inside the catalogue concern.

violations.message: assertCombineItemsRule copies the domain Order invariant 'An order requires at least one item' (also at src/domain/order.ts:27) instead of relying on that single definition.
combineItems copies the per-item validation (productId present, positive integer quantity, same message as src/domain/order.ts:30), so the same invariant exists in both application and domain.
validateCombineItems puts order-item validation (assertCombineItemsRule from order-service) in CatalogueService, mixing an order rule into the catalogue concern.
